newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks move ahead in morning, properties lead.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks move ahead in morning, properties lead.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks moved ahead in Monday morning trade, led by a bounce in property counters after they suffered heavy selling during the market's downturn last week.
The Hang Seng Index was up 93.14 points, or 0.73 percent, at 12,829.67 after tumbling 600.82 points, or 4.5 percent last week. Turnover was HK$2.43 billion after the first 40 minutes of trade.

Analysts said U.S. February producer price data, released on Friday, eased some concerns about a possible rise in interest rates at the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting on March 25. The producer price index showed a decline of 0.4 percent compared with expectations of a 0.1 percent fall.
"Right now the Fed might not have the leeway or the ability to make a preemptive move," said one trader.
However, analysts said some investors were still looking for more signs on the direction of interest rates. This week's U.S. data include February housing starts and consumer prices.
"Investors are still waiting for more signals about interest rates in the U.S.," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.
"Probably if more economic indicators show that an interest rate hike is unlikely, investors will try to buy more aggressively, but currently they will still stay on the sidelines," he added.
Property counters made the biggest gains on Monday.
"I think they are near levels where they should be accumulated for medium term investment," said So.
He said although an interest rate hike would hurt the outlook, the property market still remained active.
Henderson Land Development Co Ltd gained HK$1.00 to HK$64.00 and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd advanced HK$0.75 to HK$84.25.
Both are due to release interim results this week.

Shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd rose HK$1.25 to HK$70.25. The company said it would offer an additional 125 units at its Laguna Verde residential development at HK$8,787 per square foot, up from an initial price of HK$8,286 per square foot.
It said about 2,000 potential buyers registered to buy an initial 78 units on offer.
March Hang Seng Index futures gained 95 points to 12,785.
